residual_after_fix: The pin detects CHANGE, not GOODNESS. Still undetectable: (1) a graph and its committed pin replaced consistently by someone with local write access (the pin is only as trustworthy as the git history that carries it — it is not signed or attested); (2) a semantic truncation that stays valid JSON and is then re-pinned to its new digest by an operator (or by the same actor) — a matching pin says 'these are the bytes we pinned', not 'these bytes are complete'; (3) any path with no pin entry: unpinned/unverified and still reused, so pre-existing setups remain unprotected until someone pins them; (4) the building repo's provenance: built_at_commit records the *target* HEAD, so the graph's own build revision (and thus whether the builder was honest) is still reported stale/unverified rather than resolved; (5) no pin history, so a rollback to bytes matching a previously-pinned digest is not distinguishable from a legitimate rollback. Verifying that 2685 nodes / 7102 edges is the right graph (semantic completeness) remains outside what any digest can establish.
